lines.text: More than a thousand coral islands, barely above the waves, ruled for centuries by sultans. This is the story of the Maldives.
In 1153 the king of these Buddhist islands took up Islam, and the faith of the Maldives changed for good.
So began the sultanate, a line of rulers that would last for more than eight centuries.
In 1658 the Friday Mosque of Male was built from carved coral stone.
After a long British protectorate, in 1937 Maumoon Abdul Gayoom was born, who would rule as president for thirty years.
In 1965 the Maldives won independence from Britain, and three years later became a republic.
Mohamed Nasheed, born in 1967, would be the first freely elected president, and hold a cabinet meeting under water to warn of rising seas.
In 1978 Mohamed Muizzu was born, president since 2023.
On Boxing Day 2004 the great tsunami swept over the islands, and showed how low they lie.
And in 2018 the Sinamale Bridge linked the crowded capital, Male, to its airport island.
A nation of coral and sea, the Maldives still watches the rising tide.
